headline: Debora now needs moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing, and her spouse Kevin, the primary caregiver, reports exhaustion and is asking for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found Debora needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing. She was independent at the last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing support.
items.verifier_note: All facts match the 2026-10-26 OT note: moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, independent at last review, and the three recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting Debora out of the tub. Debora said she has been skipping showers because she is afraid of slipping.
items.verifier_note: The 2026-10-19 aide note matches: hands-on help getting out of the tub, and Debora skipping showers for fear of slipping.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin (spouse and primary caregiver) reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group.
items.verifier_note: The 2026-10-13 social work note matches every detail: exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings alone, respite request, and discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14). The pharmacist reconciled it on 2026-09-15 and updated the blister pack. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks, and no recheck is documented in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: The start date, dose, PHQ-9, pharmacist reconciliation and blister pack update, and the 4-week recheck are all in the notes and record. The cited sources contain no recheck, which matches the statement's claim that none is documented.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which began 2026-08-01. The last doses on record were 2026-04-25 and 2025-04-19.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season false, a season start of 2026-08-01, and prior doses on 2026-04-25 and 2025-04-19.

questions_for_team: How and when will bathing support be put in place (tub transfer bench, handheld shower, added home care hours), given that Debora is avoiding showers?
What respite options can start soon for Kevin, especially for evenings?
Has the 4-week sertraline recheck and a repeat PHQ-9 been done? If not, who will do it?
Is Debora's fear of slipping affecting her mood or participation, and does it need to be addressed in the care plan?
Does the PT evaluation dated 2026-10-05 still apply, given the chart correction that says the 2026-10-02 fall entry was documented on the wrong participant?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and the prior IDT review date, then pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions in the window, including reasons and discharge summaries.

Falls and near-falls check: count events in the window, injury severity, and whether any fall occurred on clopidogrel (bleeding risk) or with beta-blocker (metoprolol) related dizziness or orthostatic symptoms.

Bleeding and cardiac check given ischemic heart disease, clopidogrel and simvastatin: any chest pain, nitroglycerin spray use (frequency and dates), new bleeding, bruising, or GI bleed signs; review any new cardiology or PCP contacts.

Medication changes since last review: confirm the new sertraline start on 2026-09-13 (indication PHQ-9 of 14), check start date, dose, adherence, and any new side effects such as GI bleeding risk with clopidogrel, hyponatremia, sleep change, or falls; confirm prescriber and follow-up plan for repeat PHQ-9.

Respiratory check for COPD/chronic bronchitis and chronic sinusitis: review new albuterol or fluticasone/salmeterol use, rescue inhaler frequency, exacerbations, steroid or antibiotic courses, oxygen saturation, and inhaler technique or access problems (dry powder inhaler).

Mood and cognition: complete PHQ-9 trend and any safety screening since sertraline start, note social withdrawal, sleep, appetite, and cognitive screen results or concerns; check whether attendance at IDT or group activities changed.

Weight and nutrition trend: obesity (BMI 30+) and prediabetes history; record weights across the window, any unintentional loss or gain, and any glucose or HbA1c results and diabetes-prevention or dietary follow-up.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend on metoprolol, including any readings below threshold, orthostatic readings, and any hypotension or bradycardia documented.
Chronic pain management: pain scores over the window, opioid or analgesic changes (none listed as active; confirm any PRN or OTC use), pain interference with ADLs, and any new pain-related referrals.

Breast cancer history and thyroid: confirm surveillance imaging and oncology follow-up dates falling in or due after the window; check TSH result and levothyroxine adherence (idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism); check ADL and IADL function, caregiver or living-situation changes, and care-plan items due (advance directive, medication reconciliation, caregiver support) with owners and due dates for the IDT to discuss.
